title: How Many Grams in an Ounce of Weed? Cannabis Weights

body:
How many grams in an ounce of weed? An ounce is 28.35 grams, and dispensary menus round it to 28. Every other size on the menu is a fraction of that ounce: an eighth, a quarter and a half. Below you'll find the full chart, how far each amount goes and what Michigan law lets adults buy and keep.

## How many grams in an ounce of weed, and why menus use 28

The ounce used for cannabis is the standard U.S. ounce, which equals about 28.35 grams. A pound is 16 of those ounces, or about 453.6 grams.

Cannabis is weighed in metric grams but named in old fractions of an ounce. Rounding the ounce to 28 makes those fractions divide neatly, so an eighth becomes 3.5 grams instead of 3.54. The difference is about a third of a gram per ounce: small, but worth knowing if you compare a menu with a home scale. Licensed products state their net weight on the label, so you can always see exactly what's in the package.

## Every common weight, from a gram to a pound

| Size | Share of an ounce | Menu weight | Exact weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gram | About 1/28 | 1 g | 1 g |
| Eighth | 1/8 | 3.5 g | 3.54 g |
| Quarter | 1/4 | 7 g | 7.09 g |
| Half | 1/2 | 14 g | 14.17 g |
| Ounce | 1 | 28 g | 28.35 g |
| Pound | 16 ounces | Not sold: over the 2.5-ounce limit | 453.6 g |

For context, Michigan's 2.5-ounce limit works out to about 71 grams. For a closer look at the most popular sizes:

- [How much an eighth is](/blog/how-much-is-an-eighth-of-marijuana/)
- [What a quarter looks like](/blog/how-much-is-a-quarter-of-marijuana/)
- [The half ounce explained](/blog/how-much-is-a-half-of-marijuana/)

## What each amount looks like

Bud density varies a lot, so two packages of the same weight can look very different. A dense, tightly trimmed eighth may look half the size of an airy one. As a rough guide:

- **A gram:** one or two medium buds, enough for a couple of joints or several small bowls.
- **An eighth:** a small handful of buds that fits easily in a typical dispensary jar.
- **A quarter:** two eighths' worth, roughly a full palm.
- **A half:** enough to fill a large jar.
- **An ounce:** a substantial amount for one person, best kept in a large airtight jar.

You pay for weight, not size, so trust the label over the eye test.

## How many joints or bowls a gram makes

Researchers who analyzed more than 10,000 U.S. cannabis purchases estimated that the average joint holds about 0.32 grams. Other estimates run from roughly 0.3 to 0.5 grams, and one study put the figure at 0.66 grams. Here's the math at both ends of the common range:

| Amount | Joints at 0.5 g each | Joints at 0.3 g each |
|---|---|---|
| 1 gram | 2 | 3 |
| Eighth (3.5 g) | 7 | 11 |
| Quarter (7 g) | 14 | 23 |
| Half (14 g) | 28 | 46 |
| Ounce (28 g) | 56 | 93 |

A small pipe or bong bowl takes just a pinch, a fraction of a gram, so one gram can pack several bowls depending on their size.

## Pre-roll sizes: minis vs. full grams

Pre-rolls make the math easy, because the weight is printed on the package.

- **Full-gram pre-rolls** hold 1 gram, which is a lot for one person in one sitting.
- **Half-gram pre-rolls** hold 0.5 grams, close to what many people roll for themselves.
- **Minis** are smaller still and usually come several to a pack, which makes them easy to share or spread out.

Infused pre-rolls add concentrate to the flower, so check the label for both the weight and the THC. Our [pre-roll buyer's guide](/blog/pre-roll-buyers-guide/) compares sizes and multipacks.

## Buying tips: price per gram, and bulk vs. small sizes

- **Do the math.** Divide the price by the grams to get the price per gram, then compare across sizes and products.
- **Expect better value in bigger sizes.** Larger amounts usually cost less per gram than single grams or eighths.
- **Buy what you'll finish.** An ounce only saves money if it stays fresh until it's gone, so store it airtight, cool and dark.
- **Stack the savings.** Check our [deals](/deals/) page, and [Join The Society](/club-member-program/), our free loyalty program, to earn points on qualifying purchases. Try a new strain as an eighth before buying more.

Our guide to [shopping on a budget](/blog/cannabis-budgeting/) has more ways to save.

## What drives price in Michigan

Prices move with supply and with the product itself. A few factors matter most:

- **Quality tier:** premium buds cost more than smalls or shake from the same plants.
- **Potency and type:** high-THC flower and concentrates usually cost more per gram than everyday flower.
- **Retail taxes:** adult-use purchases carry Michigan's 10% excise tax plus the 6% sales tax. Because the sales tax is figured on the price including the excise, the two together add about 16.6%. Registered medical patients don't pay the 10% excise; only the 6% sales tax applies.
- **Wholesale tax:** as of October 2026, a 24% wholesale tax, in effect since January 1, 2026, applies when growers and processors first sell adult-use products to retailers. It isn't a line on your receipt, but wholesalers may pass the cost along.

Current prices are on your store's live menu, so check there rather than relying on averages.

## Michigan possession and purchase limits

Here's what Michigan law allows for adults 21 and older, and for registered patients:

| Situation | Limit |
|---|---|
| Buying at a licensed adult-use store | Up to 2.5 ounces per transaction, no more than 15 grams of it concentrate |
| Carrying it with you | Up to 2.5 ounces, no more than 15 grams of it concentrate |
| Keeping it at home | Up to 10 ounces, plus what your own plants produce; anything over 2.5 ounces must be locked up |
| Registered medical patients | Up to 2.5 ounces a day and 10 ounces a month from provisioning centers |

You'll need a valid photo ID issued by a government agency, since adult-use stores must check it before every sale. Keep your cannabis in Michigan, too: don't travel across state lines with cannabis. For the full rundown, see our guide to [Michigan cannabis laws](/cannabis-laws-by-state/michigan/).

faq.q: How many grams make up one ounce of cannabis?
faq.a: Exactly 28.35 grams, though dispensaries round it to 28 so the fractions divide evenly. That is why an eighth is sold as 3.5 grams, a quarter as 7 and a half as 14. The rounding works out to about a third of a gram per ounce.

faq.q: What does an eighth weigh in grams?
faq.a: An eighth is 3.5 grams on a dispensary menu, or about 3.54 grams using the exact ounce. It's a popular size because it's enough to get to know a strain before you commit to more. Depending on how you roll, an eighth makes roughly 7 to 11 joints.

faq.q: About how many joints does an ounce make?
faq.a: Somewhere between about 55 and 95, depending on how full you roll them. Research puts the average joint at around a third of a gram, while many people roll closer to half a gram. Pre-rolls print their weight on the package, which makes the math easy.

faq.q: What's the most cannabis I can buy at once in Michigan?
faq.a: Adults 21 and older can buy up to 2.5 ounces in a single transaction at a licensed adult-use store, and no more than 15 grams of that may be concentrate. Registered medical patients follow separate limits of 2.5 ounces a day and 10 ounces a month. Either way, have your photo ID with you.

faq.q: How much cannabis can I keep at home in Michigan?
faq.a: Up to 10 ounces, plus whatever your own legal home grow produces. Anything over 2.5 ounces has to be kept in a container or area with locks or other working security devices. Away from home, the limit is 2.5 ounces, with no more than 15 grams as concentrate.
